edges.description: Disordered neuronal migration is the proposed cause of the cerebellar malformation; this inference has not been tested directly.
Developmental delay reflects disordered brain development; the intermediate steps are not established.
Intellectual disability is a common, variable consequence of disordered neurodevelopment.
Speech delay, prominently expressive, is a core neurodevelopmental feature.
Autistic features occur in some individuals; the mechanism is not known.
ADHD and attention problems are among the neurodevelopmental features of the disorder; as for autism, no intermediate mechanism is established.
Vermis hypoplasia is the imaging manifestation of the malformation.
The authors attribute the predominant neurologic involvement, including ataxia, at least in part to the cerebellar malformation.

The authors attribute the predominant neurologic involvement, of which hypotonia is part, at least in part to the cerebellar malformation. This is their interpretation of a case series, not a demonstrated mechanism, and hypotonia is present from birth.
Sphincter dyssynergia produces the severe voiding dysfunction recorded as neurogenic bladder.
Voiding dysfunction is accompanied by vesicoureteral reflux in many children.
Urinary tract infections are frequent in children with voiding dysfunction and reflux.

In one series it was present in every child imaged, while other series report abnormal brain MRI in about two thirds of patients. The authors propose that the ataxia and much of the neurologic picture follow from this malformation and that the disorder be managed as a congenital nonprogressive ataxia.

nodes.description: EBF3 is required in mouse for the migration of Cajal-Retzius cells from the cortical hem and for the multipolar-to-bipolar transition of migrating neocortical neurons, through positive feedback on NeuroD1. EBF3 is also repressed by ARX, and the overlap between EBF3-related and ARX-related disorders has been taken to suggest a shared neuronal-migration mechanism. Disordered neuronal migration is the proposed basis of the cerebellar malformation and neurodevelopmental phenotype, but the evidence comes from mouse and in vitro studies.
